_doc: The operator's REAL browser environment, measured rather than invented. It exists because a fixture I invent describes the environment I imagine, and his is bigger, messier and differently shaped. Twice in two days the same harness passed every check while a defect was live on the deployed page, and both times HE found it, not the harness: first the fakes had the wrong SHAPE (register-only, where a real wallet both registers AND injects window.solana), then the wrong SIZE (two wallets against his eight). Keeping these numbers in a data file rather than in test code is the point: a number embedded in a test reads as a number someone picked, and a re-measurement should be a data edit that the harness picks up, not a code change.
_how_to_remeasure: Open the live pay page in the browser that carries his wallets, dispatch `wallet-standard:app-ready` with a register callback, wait ~1.5s, then read the collected names alongside innerWidth/innerHeight/devicePixelRatio. The browser-automation tool returns {} for an async IIFE, so use top-level await and end on a synchronous JSON.stringify.
measured_how: live pay page, operator's own connected browser profile

wallets._doc: Every Wallet Standard registration observed. ORDER IS REGISTRATION ORDER, which is what the picker sees before any hoisting.
wallets._rendered_note: Only SEVEN of the eight render on the live page: enumerateWallets filters on Solana feature presence and the real MetaMask exposes none. The harness deliberately renders all eight, because FAKE_WALLETS stamps Solana features onto every name, and eight is the worst case geometry should be asserted against. That is not a claim about what his browser shows.
wallets._corrections: An earlier invented set listed 'Brave Wallet'. It was never installed. The eighth is Petra.

geometry._doc: Measured off the live picker, not estimated. The per-row height matters more than it looks: at the earlier assumed 50px, eight rows occupy 400px and the QR clears the fold; at the real 67px they occupy about 536px, which is what makes a below-the-fold defect reachable.
geometry._scope: One viewport. The QR-below-fold defect did NOT reproduce at this size, and that is a measurement at one point rather than a general clearance.

historical_brave_measurement._doc: Kept because it stands on its own conditions and is the origin of the whole concern. The card grew 887 -> 1286 and the QR's bottom edge landed at 972 against a 900-tall viewport. His window happened to be 982 tall and cleared it by ten pixels, which is the only reason he did not hit it.

_fabrication_corrected: A viewport of 1512x982 was once attributed to him and was actually from my own test matrix. The measured truth for that incident: viewport 1000px, content 1026px, overflow 26px, scrolled 12px. He DID hit it.
